analysis.investment_thesis: Solarium Green fails the Magic Formula test: at P/E 21.5, the earnings yield is only ~4.6% — well below my 12% threshold — while ROCE of 20.1% is decent but not exceptional. It's neither cheap nor a standout compounder, which is the worst combination for a systematic value approach.
key_strengths: ROE 23% / ROCE 20.1% — respectable capital efficiency for a young company
Exposure to fast-growing Indian solar/turnkey EPC tailwind
key_risks: Earnings yield ~4.6% (1/P/E) — expensive for a civil construction EPC business
Civil construction / EPC is capital- and working-capital-intensive, which often destroys ROIC at scale
Small cap (₹301 Cr), short listed history since 2018 incorporation — ROCE sustainability unproven
red_flags: Earnings yield well below the 12% Magic Formula threshold
No multi-year ROIC track record to confirm the 20% is not a one-time spike
EPC receivables/working-capital cycles can inflate reported returns vs cash returns
analysis.detailed_analysis: Running the Magic Formula: Earnings Yield proxy = 1/21.5 ≈ 4.65% (EBIT/EV likely similar absent large net cash), which is roughly a third of what I'd want to see. ROCE of 20.1% is in the "good, not great" zone — above 15% but shy of the 25%+ bar that defines truly excellent businesses. When I rank candidates on the combined score, Solarium lands in the bottom half on cheapness and middle-of-the-pack on quality — the signature profile of a stock to skip.
